newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian court told of execution of 16 in 1978.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian court told of execution of 16 in 1978.

text.p: A prosecution witness said on Tuesday he watched a firing squad execute 16 building site labourers in Ethiopia in 1978 in front of thousands of fellow workers.

The witness, a former guardsman at the Ethiopian Patriot's Centre at Debre Zeit, 50 km (30 miles) east of Addis Ababa, was testifying at the trial of 71 former officials of Ethiopia's military junta known as the Dergue, which was toppled in 1991.

Only 46 of the 71 accused are in court in Addis Ababa. The other 25, including former Marxist leader Mengistu Haile Mariam who now lives in exile in Zimbabwe, are being tried in absentia. They are accused of genocide and crimes against humanity and face the death penalty if found guilty.

"The 16 who were suspected of being ringleaders in inciting anti-Dergue sentiments among some 1,000 labourers at the site were executed by firing squad in front of workers ordered to watch," the witness said.
"One of the 16 being executed attempted to rise after he was hit by a volley, but Mengistu's minister of construction Kassa Gabre performed a coup de grace with his pistol," he said.
The former minister is in jail awaiting trial.
The witness, who cannot be identified under court rules, said the killings at the Patriot's Centre were triggered by the killing of a leading engineer who had ordered an illegal meeting to disperse.
In the ensuing confrontation, the engineer shot dead a labourer. His comrades were so angry they beat him to death.
The witness said troops later surrounded the centre and held all workers for three days. The 16, suspected of being ring leaders, were executed in front of fellow workers, he said.
The trial was adjourned until Thursday. Prosecutors have charged 5,198 people with war crimes, homicide and genocide under the Dergue, which collapsed when Mengistu was ousted in May 1991.
